composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-110a, "24V DC SERVICE SUPPLY") is the BAE hybrid system's HVPDU/MAPS power one-line: it shows PORT and STBD HVPDU 600V DC buses feeding MAPS-1/2 converters (600V DC → 24V DC), which through isolator/contactor banks (SW1-5/SO1-5) and a 24V 110A AC/DC supply build the +24V SERVICE BUS. That bus (with SHUNT #1, fused branches F5-F9) is a distribution node feeding downstream loads named explicitly on-sheet: FWD DC PANEL, AFT DC PANEL, BILGE PUMP, FIRE PUMP, GEN START BAT., AUX SERVICE BAT. A PC CARD / BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL block with BAE/AUX selector and indicator lamps sits at bottom-left, cross-referenced to DWG 401a and DWG 114, tied into the same negative/ground bus as the loads. All equipment mapped per engineer-confirmed vocabulary and established facts (620-hvpdu identity note: 600V DC buses ARE the HVPDU, MAPS/BEL/EDN/MPCS all hang off them).

infrastructure.system_name: PORT HVPDU (600V DC bus + Q1-Q4 breakers + F1/F2 500A fuses)
facts: 600V DC bus with Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 breakers each 32A feeding downstream (to PORT MAPS-1/2)

F1 500A and F2 500A fuses (labelled F1 AUX / F2 BAT.) plus a 200Ah 24V battery tap shown at bus foot with a fused link (24V) — this appears to be a secondary low-voltage tap distinct from the main 600V bus; exact role of this 24V tap uncertain

Established identity per 620-hvpdu: PORT/STBD HVPDU is where 600V distribution starts; S1/S2 switches (not shown explicitly on this sheet) separate/select buses; this sheet shows the Q1-Q4 breaker bank + fuses for PORT side
CTB1-CTB6 = QI-POWER-485-300-LV per on-sheet legend (module part numbers for the HVPDU/MAPS converters), CTB7 = same part, marked EMERGENCY BAT.

infrastructure.system_name: STBD HVPDU (600V DC bus + Q1-Q4 breakers)
facts: Mirror of PORT HVPDU: 600V DC bus with Q1-Q4 32A breakers feeding STBD MAPS-1/2
Grounded at bus (ground symbol shown at STBD HVPDU foot)
Two converter modules, 600V DC in / 24V DC out, 2x5KW each; electronically fused and over-current protected per sheet note
Outputs via F1 250A and F2 250A fuses to CT1 and CT2 (each behind a '70' rated breaker/fuse) then onward '70' lines labeled 'to ONYX' for monitoring
Engineer-confirmed mapping MAPS-1/2 / PORT MAPS-1/2 -> 626-maps-p
Mirror of PORT MAPS-1/2: two converter modules, output via F3 250A and F4 250A fuses to CT3 and CT4, each behind '70' rated device, monitored 'to ONYX'
Engineer-confirmed mapping MAPS-1/2 -> 626-maps (STBD instance -> 626-maps-s)

infrastructure.system_name: Isolator/Contactor bank (SW1-SW5 / SO1-SO5) between MAPS outputs and +24V Service Bus
facts: 5 isolator switches SW1-SW5 each drive a corresponding solenoid contactor SO1-SO5
This bank sits between the PORT/STBD MAPS 24V DC outputs (via CT1-CT5) and the SHUNT #1 / +24V SERVICE BUS junction — infrastructure distribution hardware, not itself a piece of equipment
CT5 present on SW5 branch, also tapped 'to ONYX'

infrastructure.system_name: +24V Service Bus (distribution bus with SHUNT #1 and F5-F9 fused outgoing branches)
facts: Bus fed from isolator/contactor bank (SO1-SO5) through SHUNT #1 (500A/50mV) used for current measurement
T/S S terminal strip cross-references 'see DWG 413' and 'BAE VOLTAGE SENCE' tap for BAE voltage sensing off this bus

Outgoing fused branches: F5 100A (SW6/FWD DC PANEL), F6 200A (SW7/AFT DC PANEL), F7 60A (SW8/BILGE PUMP), F8 60A (SW9/FIRE PUMP), F9 125A (SW10, further load — see DWG 110b, CT6 to ONYX / LV. BAE PANEL)
SW11 + F16 250A branch feeds AUX SERVICE BAT. and 'to GEN. START BAT.' via SO 9

infrastructure.system_name: 24V 110A AC/DC power supply (230V AC in / 24V DC 185A out)
facts: Standalone 230V AC (L/N in) to 24V DC 185A converter, fused by F18 125A on the DC output, feeding the T/S S terminal strip / Re1 / Re2 relay logic area used for BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode) signalling
Cross-referenced to Re 2a on DWG 113 and BAE START KEY SW / LV. BAE PANEL wording
Not clearly one of the named CTB/MAPS units; treated as infrastructure supply for the BAE control-relay logic on this sheet since no dedicated equipment node names it

infrastructure.system_name: PC CARD / BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL enclosure
facts: Dotted-boundary enclosure with numbered I/O terminals 1-10 (left and right strips), a 5-lamp indicator bank, and a BAE/AUX rotary selector switch
Labeled 'BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL', cross-referenced to DWG 401a; terminal legends AUX/BAE/NEG/+EM at bottom of left strip
Cross-referenced 'to ON/OFF SW, see DWG 114' and 'see DWG 114' for PC CARD detail — control loop for BEL units continues off-sheet
Ties into NEGATIVE BUS / 230V AC GROUND (=SHIPS GROUND) bar running along the bottom of the sheet

infrastructure.system_name: Negative Bus / 230V AC Ground bar (bottom of sheet)
facts: Common negative/ground bar spanning bottom of sheet with drop tags to FWD DC PANEL, AFT DC PANEL, BILGE PUMP, FIRE PUMP, GEN START BAT., EMERGENCY BAT., AUX SERVICE BAT.
Labeled '230V AC GROUND (=SHIPS GROUND)' at the right end, tying AC ground and DC negative together on this bar
T/S E terminal + QE7 6A breaker branch feeds 'to +24V EMERGENCY POWER' off this same lower zone

uncertainties: 24V 110A/230V AC/185A converter: not matched to a named equipment node (no CTB/MAPS tag on it); its exact ownership (dedicated BAE control supply vs. general service supply) is inferred as infrastructure feeding the Re1/Re2 relay logic — flagged rather than forced onto an equipment node.

Re1 and Re2 relay coil energising paths (switch1-4 -> relay coil -> output) are drawn but the exact downstream destination of each relay's output line (right side) is not legible/traced beyond 'to Re 2a (see DWG 113)' and 'BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode)' labels — off-sheet continuation only.

PC CARD internal wiring (terminals 2-5, R2-R5) and the AUX/BAE selector-to-lamp-bank wiring is present in the extraction as internal connections but the exact per-lamp assignment (which lamp indicates which state) is not labeled on the sheet.

F1 AUX / F2 BAT. small fused link near PORT HVPDU foot with a 200Ah tap and 24V label: relationship of this to the main 600V DC bus vs. a separate low-voltage circuit is unclear from the drawing; not assigned a definite role.
SW10 branch (F9 125A) destination beyond 'see DWG 110b' / CT6 / LV. BAE PANEL is not fully resolved on this sheet — continuation is off-sheet per the cross-reference.
